correctness.rationale: The definition quantifies all shortest paths with both endpoints inside S or outside S. In T_n of diameter two, both selected and unselected neighbors of each selected vertex must induce cliques, because any nonadjacent pair forms a forbidden geodesic through the selected vertex. For n>=5 the neighborhood K_(n-2) square K_2 has clique number n-2 and only the two side cliques attain it; their disjoint partition forces an entire root star. An extra selected root edge avoiding its center creates a forbidden length-two geodesic. Converse: a full star is a clique, and its complement of edges avoiding the center is geodesically convex. At n=4 the neighbor C4 forces every selected vertex to lie in a triangle component, yielding eight triangles; n=3 is complete and all subsets qualify. Independently enumerated all subsets at n=3..6 with shortest-path definition, matching all coefficients; the unlimited theorem rests on the structural argument. The comparison with ordinary gp uses the published n mod 3 theorem and credits it.
